---
title: "History"
subtitle: "What public sources show so far — and what they do not"
---

The chapters below start before CSIL existed as a named program. They look at earlier housing and support arrangements, then at CSIL’s early years and later changes.

This site uses one possible order of events so later evidence has a place to land. It is a reading aid, **not** a claim that each step officially became the next:

**care in institutions or through agencies → independent-living experiments led by disabled people → Creekview → the Enhanced Consumer Participation Model (ECPM) → funding that followed the person → CSIL designed and piloted → a province-wide program.**

No page treats Creekview → ECPM → CSIL as a proven official sequence. The chapters below reconstruct what public sources now support and label what they do not.

## State of the evidence {#state-of-the-evidence}

### Well established (from public sources this archive has read, or from a bibliography that lists them)

- Creekview existed as a mid-1980s community residence for a small group of men with high-level, mostly ventilator-dependent quadriplegia. It was planned by February 1984 and in place by April 1986 ([Creekview](creekview.qmd)).
- A 1990 ECPM *Skill Development Manual* (BC Rehab and Greater Vancouver Home Support Society; five modules) is independently listed in the Roeher / Salisbury bibliography. The manual itself has not been read ([ECPM](ecpm.qmd)).
- By late 1995 a Ministry of Health program publicly named Choice in Supports for Independent Living existed. A union newspaper described it as new or a pilot, housed in Community Support Branch / Continuing Care Division ([HEU *Guardian* Nov/Dec 1995](../sources/1995-heu-guardian-novdec.qmd)).
- A November 2008 CSIL Program Review Synthesis Report exists and has been read as an Internet Archive Microlog fiche. It dates CSIL only to “the 1990's.”
- Current ministry policy defines CSIL employer, client support group, and CSIL representative ([HCC Policy 4.C](../sources/hcc-policy-manual-4c.qmd)). Those are present rules, not recovered 1990s documents.

### Later accounts (not records from the 1980s or 1990s)

- SCI BC and journalistic accounts of Creekview residents, of people “championing” the project, and of the spelling “Creekside.”
- IFRC and Gauthier materials that name ECPM as a step before CSIL and that call CSIL “established” in 1993 or 1994.
- The 2012 Ombudsperson report’s pairing of **pilot 1994** and **province-wide 1995**, including later wording that mid-1990s policy already contemplated a client support group.
- Order of Canada “Initiator” language for Paul Gauthier (an official honour, not a 1990s file).

### Unresolved / missing

- Formal succession from Creekview to ECPM to CSIL.
- The full text of the 1990 ECPM manual, and whether any 1994 ECPM training manual is a distinct document. The evidence is not clear enough to decide.
- *Keys on Freedom* (title, author, and year still come only from early project notes).
- Original 1993–95 Ministry of Health design and pilot records.
- A single founding year. Later official records give 1994 and 1995 different meanings (pilot, then province-wide). A later source uses 1993. A 1995 newspaper still said new/pilot and does not confirm that a province-wide rollout was finished.
- The 1987 Creekview evaluation report (known to have existed; copy still sought).
- Whether the Ombudsperson’s “provincial review in 2007” is the 2008 synthesis.
